'''Clara Y. Lim-Sylianco''' (18 August 1925 – 23 July 2013<ref name=":0"/>) was a Filipino [[chemist]] who was granted the title of [[National Scientist of the Philippines]] in 1994. Lim-Sylianco's research focused on [[mutagen]]s, [[antimutagen]]s, and bio-organic mechanisms. She has published articles, books, and monographs in [[organic chemistry]], [[biochemistry]], genetic [[toxicology]], and molecular nutrition. Also an educator, Lim-Sylianco has written books that are used as reference texts in college chemistry courses in the Philippines.

== Education ==
Lim-Sylianco received an associate degree for the pre-medicine program at [[Silliman University]] in 1947. However, she switched out of the Medicine track shortly after to pursue a bachelor's degree in chemistry, where she graduated as ''magna cum laude'' in 1949''.''<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|url=http://www.nast.ph/images/pdf%20files/Publications/Annual%20Reports/Academy%20News%201980%20Vol.%202%20No.%202.pdf|title=Academy News Vol. 2 No. 2|publisher=National Academy of Science and Technology|location=Philippines|pages=3}}</ref> Lim-Sylianco then pursued a master's in Chemistry at [[University of the Philippines]]{{Which|date=August 2025}} in 1949. There, she worked as a research assistant until 1951 and later took on an instructor role until she graduated in 1953.<ref name=":0" /> After receiving a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright]] scholarship, she went to the United States to pursue her doctoral studies in biochemistry and organic chemistry at the [[University of Iowa]].<ref name=":1" /> She was a research assistant in the university's Department of Pediatrics from 1953 to 1955 and a research fellow in the Department of Biochemistry from 1955 to 1957.<ref name=":0" />

== Career and research ==
Lim-Sylianco moved back to teach at the chemistry and biochemistry departments of the University of the Philippines in 1957. From 1970 to 1973, she served as a consultant for the National Institute of Science and Technology.<ref name=":0" /> Lim-Sylianco was a prolific researcher, making contributions to several fields such as environmental mutagens and anti-mutagens, biochemical nutrition, bioorganic mechanisms, and mutagenicity of Philippine medical plants (trilaurin, trilinolein, etc.).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=National Scientist: Clara Lim-Sylianco|url=https://members.nast.ph/index.php/list-of-national-scientist/details/3/26#honors-and-awards-received|website=National Academy of Science and Technology}}</ref> In 1989, she became a member of the International Advisory Committee on Anti-mutagens. She was also dedicated to chemical education and wrote textbooks on organic chemistry and molecular biochemistry that were adopted nationally. These include: ''Principle of Organic Chemistry, 5th ed.,'' 1975; ''Modern Biochemistry'', 1976; ''Monograph Series on Molecular Biochemistry: Nucleic Acids, Protein, Carbohydrates, Lipids'', 1974; ''Laboratory Manual in Organic Chemistry'', 1965; and ''Laboratory Manual in Biochemistry'', 1961.<ref name=":0" />

== Awards and recognition ==
In 1958, she became a Fellow of the Royal Society.<ref name=":1" />

In 1977, she received the [[Gregorio Y. Zara|Gregario Y. Zara]] Award.

From 1974 to 1977, she was the University of the Philippines Endowment Professional Chair in Chemistry.

She was recognized as a [[National Scientist of the Philippines]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Briefer on the Order of National Scientists|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/briefer-on-the-order-of-national-scientist/|website=Official Gazette|access-date=2020-11-12|archive-date=2020-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201117061117/https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/briefer-on-the-order-of-national-scientist/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
